adr_divergence.claim: manifest, environment, pinned dependencies, ordered execution trace and artifact hashes
adr_divergence.reading: the ADR's bundle description names artifact hashes among five elements; the manifest now carries a `files` list with one sha256 and one byte count per archived file, so the element is present in the export a visitor keeps and the divergence this reading recorded in its first pass no longer holds

events.detail: returns sha256 equal to the written bytes (True) and verified=True: the tool writes one payload, reads the file back, and raises rather than report a digest the file does not hold; the instrument re-read 3 lines including the header on its own account

returns ['artifact_id', 'bytes', 'metadata', 'path', 'sha256', 'type']; sha256 matches the file it wrote (True) and is also recorded under metadata.sha256, so the run record inherits the field; the writer reads the bytes back and raises on a mismatch

40 entries across 8 committed records; top-level fields ['created_at', 'created_by', 'id', 'metadata', 'path', 'type']; 40 of 40 carry metadata.sha256 -- the field SaveArtifactTool writes from the bytes it re-read -- and the paths name a gitignored artifact root, so the digest is checkable by whoever holds the file and is not re-checked here

manifest keys ['artifact_root', 'excluded', 'files', 'included', 'run_id', 'storage']; 2 of 2 archived files carry a sha256, and every digest equals the bytes the zip holds (mismatches []); the deleted entry lands in excluded rather than in the archive, so two bundles of different bytes now differ in their manifests

returns the digest beside the text rather than inside it (True); the strip rule still holds over the same bytes -- a 64-hex token in the objective is removed (True) while the figure 0.81 survives -- so recording the digest did not weaken the rule that cleans the prose
48 committed exports parsed by class [('json', 40), ('md', 8)]; the parser decides readability, nothing compares it with a stored digest

not_claimed: no containment and no tamper resistance: a digest nobody compares is a number, not a control
no claim about the bundle's environment, pinned dependencies or execution trace; this reading examines digests and parse results only
no claim that an absent digest means a corrupt file, and no claim that a parsed file is correct

one export-side digest is declared rather than compared here: the 40 committed artifact records name files under a gitignored root, so this instrument counts the field and cannot re-open what it names
not_measured is not zero: csv, png and xlsx have no committed export to read
publication_ready is untouched here and keeps its own gate

procedure: Run `python scripts/measure_export_lifecycle.py --record > docs/audit/export-lifecycle.json` in the repository root.
Run `python scripts/measure_export_lifecycle.py --verify` to rebuild every field from the tree and compare it with the record.
The instrument writes into throwaway temporary directories only; nothing under the repository is written by it.

The 40 committed artifact records were backfilled once by `scripts/backfill_artifact_digests.py`, which reads each file it names and prints the digest it computed; the record it writes is the input, and re-running it is what a reader does to check the numbers.
